thread:
maria: Heads up — started seeing a provisioning backlog in us-west-2 for GPU nodes ~10m ago. Autoscaler loops are creating instances but they stay in PROVISIONING. Logs show KMS decrypt failures from the bootstrap agent.
jonathan: seeing same. Errors: `AccessDeniedException: KMS:Decrypt` on instance-profile role when trying to unwrap disk key. Looks like a key policy change?
ops-bot: deploy/infra-autoscaler v1.9.2 reported 87 provisioning failures in 12m on cluster-gpu-usw2.
samir: @maria can you paste the exact error snippet?
maria: log snippet: `2026-03-18T16:12:03Z ERROR bootstrap: failed to decrypt disk key: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/provisioner-role/i-06abc123 is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/abcd-ef01-2345`
elaine: that KMS key is the cluster LUKS key we rolled over yesterday as part of the quarterly rotation. I updated the key policy to be more restrictive (remove account-wide principal) — probably related.
jonathan: okay, that matches. Autoscaler uses instance profile `provisioner-role`. The new key policy might not include that role's assume-role principal.
infra-oncall: impact: ~25% of GPU pool capacity stuck provisioning -> some jobs get queued or routed to lower-tier nodes; cost spike due to churn (instances stuck then terminated).
maria: quick mitigation idea: re-add old key policy permissions to allow `arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/provisioner-role` kms:Decrypt for that key, then requeue nodes. Can someone with KMS perms revert?
elaine: I can do a scoped rollback. Will regrant kms:Decrypt + kms:Encrypt + kms:GenerateDataKey for the role principal for the key alias `alias/cluster-usw2-gpu`. Doing it now.
ops-bot: auditlog event: user=elaine action=UpdateKeyPolicy resource=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/abcd-ef01-2345 time=2026-03-18T16:21:10Z
samir: after the policy change, start a couple of dummy nodes to validate. maria can you re-run one bootstrap?
maria: re-triggered provisioning for i-test-001. Logs now show successful decrypt -> `kms:Decrypt succeeded` and disk formatted. Instance moved to RUNNING at 16:24:33Z.
jonathan: nice. But we should not leave the key policy wide-open. Propose we introduce a KMS alias-per-role mapping and update the provisioning flow to cache allowed key ARNs so we can rotate without rollbacks. Also add an automated policy test in the rotation job.
elaine: agree. For now I'll add a policy statement with a condition limiting decryption to `arn:aws:sts::111222333444:assumed-role/provisioner-role/*` and only for the `Encrypt`/`Decrypt` actions. Then rotate again in a test account.
infra-oncall: FYI: CloudTrail shows a 30s gap in PutObject audit logs to our S3 audit-bucket during the rotation window; likely unrelated but raising.
maria: that's worrying — if audit events are delayed or dropped we lose compliance visibility. jonathan can you check S3 bucket policy and the CloudTrail delivery status for that time?
jonathan: checking CloudTrail console now — deliveryStatus shows 1 failed attempt 16:16:xx due to `AccessDenied` on the S3 PutObject because the bucket policy had a deny for non-SSL which the trail tried to use? strange. Posting snippet: `CloudTrail: PutObject failed, s3:ObjectPut: AccessDenied, requester=cloudtrail.amazonaws.com`
samir: Could be the rotation workflow changed the bucket's ACL/lock or we rolled out a new bucket policy yesterday. Who touched the S3 audit-bucket?
elaine: that was me, updated bucket policy to block public access and restrict some principals. I thought CloudTrail used the same principal but maybe I filtered it. I'll revert the minimal part that's blocking cloudtrail.
maria: let's be careful — don't revert everything. We need (1) CloudTrail delivery allowed, (2) KMS policy tightened for provisioner, (3) run post-change integration tests.
jonathan: I'll add a small automated check in our infra CI: create a test S3 PutObject as cloudtrail principal and verify kms decrypt permission for test role. Can have a synthetic audit event generation step.
infra-oncall: ops impact summary: 16:10–16:25 provisioning backlog, ~200 GPU-minutes lost due to churn, temporary job routing to smaller nodes, no data plane compromise. Compliance impact: ~30s of delayed audit delivery (logged).
samir: follow-ups — (a) elaine to push scoped KMS policy and then rotate in staging, (b) jonathan to add CI checks and cloudtrail S3 policy test, (c) maria to run a smoke scale test post-rollback, (d) infra-oncall to file an incident ticket with timeline and cost estimate.
elaine: done: policy updated and staged. Link to diff: https://internal.redwood/infrastructure/changes/PR-8243
maria: smoke scale test passed (created 8 nodes, all bootstrapped). No further decrypt errors.
infra-oncall: filing incident: INC-2026-0318-56, attaching logs + cost calc ~ $120 for churn.
jonathan: I'll also add a runbook blurb to the KMS rotation playbook: test provisioning with `provisioner-role` and check CloudTrail delivery.
maria: thanks team. Let's have a retro next week to tighten rotation gating so this doesn't recur. :thumbsup:
